checkpoints.timeZeroRule: The training-turn-0 snapshot is a uniform/missing-history diagnostic, not an independent confirmatory observation. It contributes no dyad-level confirmatory statistic.

claimBoundary: This is a deferred future-study draft (R12). It authorizes no run, no allocation, and no confirmatory reuse of LV01 or development outcomes. Progression requires valid learnable task/replay machinery from LV01 R09 evidence and a separate prospective allocation.

equalContentUnsignedHistory.access: Identical numerical payload and update schedule as the current sparse ledger at each checkpoint, without authentication. Predictions must match the current ledger exactly; isolates authentication overhead and detection.

finalLedgerRetrospective.access: Full final-training ledger applied to earlier checkpoints.
finalLedgerRetrospective.rule: A final ledger used to explain earlier actions is a labeled retrospective diagnostic, never a prospective competitor. It enters no confirmatory statistic.

latestSparseLedger.access: Latest authenticated sparse ledger strictly before each checkpoint cutoff.

oneCheckpointStaleLedger.access: Latest authenticated sparse ledger strictly before the previous checkpoint cutoff (for checkpoint 750, the turn-0 empty history).

ordinaryRecords.access: Only preceding ordinary records (observations, delivered tokens, actions) before each checkpoint; no ledger, policy, or future data.

periodicFullSnapshots.access: Full 32-by-16 association snapshots at fixed cadence: every 64 training episodes plus the five LV02 cutoffs, matching LV01 v2.

evaluation.commitmentRule: Commit all predictor probability vectors, predictor versions and fitted digests, probe case and candidate identities, delivered-message schedule, ledger cutoffs, policy and state digests, and action-draw commitments before the first probe receiver action at each checkpoint. Hashing inputs alone is insufficient.
evaluation.exclusionRule: Probe cases are excluded from training and from all predictor fitting except the declared preceding-data windows. Probe outcomes never update policy, optimizer, checkpoint, or ledger state.
evaluation.roleBalance: Receiver-role and eligible-target balanced within each checkpoint probe set, as in LV01 v2.
evaluation.sharedActionRandomness: Each probe case uses one privately derived uniform draw, disclosed to the auditor after sealing. Sampling uses a fixed candidate order and inverse CDF; the draw never enters any learner observation or prediction function.
evaluation.stateRule: At each checkpoint freeze the full dyad state (both policies, optimizers, recurrent states, ledger cutoff). Restore that frozen checkpoint state before every probe case. Probe evaluation does not feed learning.

execution.iterationBoundary: The five-iteration lifetime allowance is not renewed by this draft; LV02 needs its own lawful prospective allocation before any collection.
execution.releaseSchedule: none; no artificial one-second release padding in this declared Prototype profile

forbidden: policy updates during any probe evaluation

observationSchemas.claimBoundary: Code-path and input-boundary checks must establish this restriction for these cooperative learners. This is logical separation under a trusted process and operator, not resistance to a malicious shared-process agent.
predictorForbidden: true probe target in ordinary-record fits
final-ledger content in any prospective predictor

pilotRule: LV02 receives its own dedicated prospective pilot of twenty valid dyads and its own sample-size selection under the generalized selector (m=k=1). No confirmatory reuse of LV01 or development outcomes.

primaryContrast.statistic: Mean pre-action multiclass Brier loss of the one-checkpoint-stale ledger minus the current ledger across the four post-training checkpoints (750, 1500, 2250, 3000), with equal checkpoint and receiver-role weights within dyad.

progressionGate.favorableFindingNotRequired: Progression requires valid learnable task and replay machinery from LV01 R09 evidence, not a favorable LV-U finding.
progressionGate.noCommunicationRule: If the earlier valid LV01 study shows no learned communication, complete its report and document why this unchanged task cannot yet answer a developmental-language claim. Any learner or task redesign is a new prospective study, never a retry of nulls.
requires: R09 valid evidence for the shared task/learner/replay machinery
separate prospective LV02 allocation and registration

question: When two separately learning agents acquire a useful symbolic convention in one fixed referential task, do contemporaneous ledger records predict near-future receiver behavior better than one-checkpoint-stale records, and how does that value change as meanings develop across training checkpoints?
scopeBoundary: One synthetic numeric referential task, one recurrent scratch-RL learner family, one fixed-token carrier: the LV01 v2 task/learner/carrier unchanged.
Prototype Mode probe collection only; no hostile-process, timing-channel, or deployment-isolation claim.
No compositionality, grounding, human-audit, public-timestamp, independent-review, or full-program completion claim.
The original E00-E50 protocols, their experiment IDs, all LV01 bytes, and all v1/v2 semantics remain unchanged. LV02 never marks any original card complete by resemblance.

secondaryContrasts.informationAccess: Information access for every secondary comparator stays explicit; richer-information gains are described as such, never as authentication effects.
list: Ordinary-record predictors versus the current ledger at each checkpoint (preceding-data only).
Periodic full association snapshots versus the sparse current ledger (freshness versus sparsity).
Coverage, update age, distribution drift missed without argmax changes, retained bytes, and future-action Brier loss at each checkpoint.

task.claimBoundary: Fresh probe cases are not new-type generalization or compositionality evidence.
task.duplicateRule: Canonical scenario content and IDs are distinct across training, all probe sets, and all LV01 partitions after outcome-free rederivation.
